**Clinical Note Template**

1. **Patient Information**

Name: Arthur Miller
Age/Gender: 65/Male
Hospital Stay Dates: October 26, 2023 to November 15, 2023 (with intermittent discharges and readmissions)
Admitting Diagnosis:  Suspected colorectal cancer with bowel obstruction
Discharge Diagnosis: Stage IIB adenocarcinoma of the colon, postoperative ileus, anemia

2. **Visit Details**

**[October 26, 2023, 14:30]**

Provider Role: Emergency Physician
Reason for Visit: Severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, inability to pass stool for 3 days.
Interventions:  Complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), abdominal X-ray, CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis.
Findings/Results: CBC revealed mild anemia (Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL). CMP showed mild dehydration. Abdominal X-ray showed significant distension of the bowel. CT scan revealed a large mass in the sigmoid colon causing near-complete bowel obstruction with evidence of stranding suggesting inflammation.
Treatment Plan:  Intravenous fluids (IVFs) for dehydration, nasogastric (NG) tube placement for decompression, bowel rest, and urgent surgical consultation.


**[October 26, 2023, 18:00]**

Provider Role: General Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Emergency surgical consultation for bowel obstruction.
Interventions:  Physical exam, review of imaging studies.
Findings/Results: Confirmed findings of the Emergency Physician.  Significant risk of bowel perforation.
Treatment Plan:  Scheduled for emergent sigmoid colectomy with possible ileostomy.


**[October 27, 2023, 08:00]**

Provider Role: General Surgeon & Anesthesiologist
Reason for Visit:  Sigmoid colectomy.
Interventions:  Sigmoid colectomy with end-to-end anastomosis.  Placement of a Jackson-Pratt drain.
Findings/Results:  Surgery completed without significant complications.  Specimen sent for pathology.
Treatment Plan:  Postoperative care in the surgical ICU, IV antibiotics (Cefazolin), pain management (Morphine PCA), NG tube to remain in situ.


**[October 28, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Surgical ICU Physician
Reason for Visit: Postoperative monitoring.
Interventions:  Vital signs monitoring, assessment of surgical site, assessment of bowel sounds, IV fluids, pain medication administration.
Findings/Results:  Stable vital signs, minimal surgical site drainage, absent bowel sounds, mild ileus noted.
Treatment Plan:  Continue current treatment plan.


**[October 30, 2023, 14:00]**

Provider Role: Surgical ICU Physician
Reason for Visit:  Persistent ileus, abdominal distension.
Interventions:  Abdominal examination, repeat abdominal X-ray.
Findings/Results:  Significant abdominal distension noted.  X-ray showed persistent air-fluid levels suggestive of ongoing ileus.
Treatment Plan:  Continue bowel rest, increase intravenous fluids, consider prokinetic medication (Metoclopramide).


**[November 2, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role: Surgical ICU Physician
Reason for Visit:  Improved bowel function.
Interventions:  Abdominal examination, removal of NG tube.
Findings/Results:  Improved bowel sounds, passage of flatus.
Treatment Plan:  Advance diet as tolerated, discontinue IV fluids, continue pain medication as needed.  Transfer to general ward.


**[November 7, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Physician (General Medicine)
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up post-surgery, anemia.
Interventions:  Physical examination, review of pathology report, CBC.
Findings/Results:  Pathology confirmed Stage IIB adenocarcinoma of the colon.  CBC showed persistent anemia (Hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL).
Treatment Plan:  Iron supplementation (Ferrous sulfate).  Referral to Oncology for further treatment planning.  Discharge planned for tomorrow.


**[November 8, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Physician (General Medicine)
Reason for Visit:  Discharge planning.
Interventions:  Review discharge instructions.
Findings/Results:  Patient clinically stable.
Treatment Plan:  Discharge to home.


**[November 12, 2023, 15:00]**

Provider Role: Emergency Physician
Reason for Visit:  Return to hospital due to severe abdominal pain, fever, and chills.
Interventions:  CBC, CMP, blood cultures, abdominal CT scan.
Findings/Results:  Leukocytosis (WBC 16,000/µL), elevated CRP, positive blood cultures for *E. coli*.  CT scan showed a small amount of fluid around the surgical site, suggestive of a possible abscess.
Treatment Plan:  IV antibiotics (Piperacillin-tazobactam), surgical consultation.


**[November 13, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: General Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Evaluation of suspected surgical site infection.
Interventions:  Physical examination, ultrasound-guided drainage of a small pericolic abscess.
Findings/Results:  Successful drainage of the abscess.  Culture sent for sensitivity testing.
Treatment Plan:  Continue IV antibiotics, close monitoring for further complications.


**[November 15, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Physician (General Medicine)
Reason for Visit:  Discharge planning.
Interventions:  Review of hospital course, medication reconciliation, discharge instructions.
Findings/Results:  Patient improving clinically, afebrile, improved appetite.
Treatment Plan:  Discharge to home with instructions for outpatient wound care and follow-up appointments.


3. **Key Events During Hospitalization**

* Emergent sigmoid colectomy on October 27, 2023, due to bowel obstruction caused by colorectal cancer.
* Postoperative ileus requiring prolonged bowel rest and intravenous fluids.
* Development of a surgical site infection requiring percutaneous drainage and intravenous antibiotics.
* Diagnosis of Stage IIB adenocarcinoma of the colon.

4. **Ongoing Management and Care**

Throughout his hospitalization, Mr. Miller received intravenous fluids, pain management (Morphine PCA initially, then oral analgesics), antibiotics (Cefazolin initially, then Piperacillin-tazobactam), and iron supplementation.  He had regular monitoring of vital signs, surgical site, bowel sounds, and laboratory values. He received nutritional support via intravenous fluids and then a gradual progression to a regular diet.  Consultations with Oncology were arranged for further cancer treatment planning.

5. **Discharge Summary**

Discharge Medications:  Ferrous sulfate 325mg PO BID, Acetaminophen 500mg PO Q4-6h prn pain,  Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BID for 7 days (for surgical site infection prophylaxis).

Follow-up Instructions:  Follow-up appointment with General Surgery in one week for wound assessment.  Follow-up appointment with Oncology in two weeks for cancer treatment planning.  Outpatient wound care as needed.

Prognosis:  Guarded.  While the immediate post-operative course was complicated by ileus and infection, the patient is now clinically stable.  The long-term prognosis depends on the success of future cancer treatment.
